easy.def: A woman who washed clothes for her job.
examples: The washerwoman washed clothes.
A washerwoman worked at the river.
The washerwoman hung the sheets.

more.def: A woman who earned money by washing clothes, especially long ago.
examples: The washerwoman scrubbed shirts by the river.
In the old days, a washerwoman did laundry for rich families.
The washerwoman hung sheets on the line.

easy.def: A room with a toilet and a sink.
examples: Where is the washroom?
The washroom is clean.
I need the washroom.

more.def: A room with a sink and a toilet, also called a bathroom or restroom.
examples: Excuse me, where is the washroom?
The washroom is down the hall on the left.
Wash your hands in the washroom before lunch.

easy.def: A table that holds a bowl of water for washing.
examples: The washstand is in the bedroom.
A washstand has a bowl.
The washstand is wood.

more.def: A piece of furniture that held a basin and jug of water for washing, used before indoor plumbing.
examples: In the old days, a washstand stood in the bedroom.
The washstand held a bowl and a jug.
A towel hung beside the washstand.

easy.def: A big tub for washing clothes.
examples: She washed clothes in a washtub.
The washtub is big.
Water is in the washtub.

more.def: A large tub in which clothes were washed by hand.
examples: Grandma washed clothes in a big washtub.
The washtub was filled with soapy water.
The children splashed in the washtub.

easy.def: A flying insect with a thin waist that can sting.
examples: A wasp stung me.
The wasp has stripes.
A wasp built a nest.

more.def: A flying insect with a narrow waist and yellow and black stripes that can sting, and often builds a paper nest.
examples: A wasp built a paper nest under the roof of our porch.
The wasp buzzed around the picnic table.
Wasps look like bees, but they have thinner bodies.

easy.def: To use too much of something.
examples: Do not waste water.
I wasted my time.
She wastes paper.

more.def: To use something carelessly or for no good reason.
examples: Turn off the tap so you do not waste water.
He wasted the whole morning playing games.
We waste less food when we plan our meals.

easy.def: Things you throw away.
examples: Put waste in the bin.
Waste goes to the dump.
Food waste goes in the compost.

more.def: Things that are thrown away because they are no longer wanted.
examples: The truck takes our waste to the dump.
Plastic waste can hurt sea animals.
We sort our waste into recycling and trash.

easy.def: A small can for trash.
examples: Throw it in the wastebasket.
The wastebasket is full.
The wastebasket is under the desk.

more.def: A small container for throwing away paper and other small trash.
examples: I threw the paper in the wastebasket.
The wastebasket was under the desk.
She emptied the wastebasket every day.

easy.def: Using more than needed.
examples: It is wasteful to leave the tap on.
A wasteful habit.
Throwing food away is wasteful.

more.def: Using more than is needed or throwing away useful things.
examples: It is wasteful to leave the water running.
Throwing out good food is wasteful.
Too much packaging is wasteful.

easy.def: Land that is empty and bare, where nothing grows.
examples: The desert was a wasteland.
Nothing grew in the wasteland.
The wasteland was dry.

more.def: Empty land that has been spoiled or is too dry or bare for crops.
examples: The dry wasteland stretched for miles.
Nothing grew in the barren wasteland.
The old factory site was a wasteland of weeds and broken bricks.

easy.def: Paper that you throw away.
examples: Put it in the wastepaper basket.
The wastepaper is full.
He threw out the wastepaper.

more.def: Paper that has been used and is to be thrown away.
examples: She put the scrap in the wastepaper basket.
The wastepaper was collected for recycling.
The room was full of crumpled wastepaper.

easy.def: Dirty water that has been used.
examples: Wastewater goes to a plant.
Clean the wastewater.
It is wastewater.

more.def: Water that has been used and is dirty, such as water from sinks, tubs and drains.
examples: Wastewater flows to a cleaning plant.
The factory must clean its wastewater.
Wastewater from the sinks goes down the drain.

easy.def: To look at something for a while.
examples: I watch the birds.
We watched a movie.
Watch me jump.

more.def: To look carefully at something for a while.
examples: We sat on the dock and watched the boats go by.
She watched the chef roll out the dough.
Watch the clock so we do not miss the bus.

easy.def: A small clock you wear on your wrist.
examples: I got a new watch.
His watch says noon.
She looks at her watch.

more.def: A small clock that you wear on your wrist.
examples: He checked his watch to see if it was time for lunch.
My grandfather gave me his old watch.
The watch ticked quietly on her wrist.

easy.def: A dog that guards a place.
examples: The watchdog barked.
Our watchdog stays near the gate.
A watchdog guards the farm.

more.def: A dog kept to guard a house or land and bark if a stranger comes.
examples: The watchdog barked when someone came to the gate.
A large watchdog slept beside the barn door.
Our watchdog guards the yard at night.

easy.def: A person who makes or fixes watches.
examples: The watchmaker fixed my watch.
A watchmaker uses tiny tools.
The watchmaker is skilled.

more.def: A person whose job is to make and repair watches and clocks.
examples: The watchmaker fixed Grandpa's old watch.
A watchmaker uses tiny tools and a magnifying glass.
The watchmaker opened the back of the clock.

easy.def: A person who guards a building at night.
examples: The watchman walked around.
A watchman guards the store.
The watchman checked the doors.

more.def: A person whose job is to guard a building or a place, especially at night.
examples: The watchman walked around the warehouse with a flashlight each night.
In the old town, the watchman called out the hours from the tower.
The watchman locked the gates when everyone had gone home.

easy.def: A tall tower for watching a wide area.
examples: A guard stood in the watchtower.
The watchtower is high.
We climbed the watchtower.

more.def: A high tower from which people watch for danger over a wide area.
examples: Rangers in the watchtower spotted smoke in the forest.
The fire watchtower rose above the trees.
We climbed the watchtower to see the valley.

easy.def: What falls as rain and fills rivers and oceans.
examples: I drink water.
The water is cold.
Fish live in water.

more.def: The clear liquid that falls as rain, fills rivers and oceans, and is needed by all living things.
examples: Plants and animals need water to live.
The water in the lake was cold and clear.
We filled our bottles with water before the hike.

easy.def: To give plants a drink.
examples: I water the plants.
She watered the garden.
Dad waters the lawn.

more.def: To give plants or soil a drink so they can grow.
examples: We water the tomato plants every morning.
He watered the flowers with a green can.
The farmer waters the crops during the dry summer.

easy.def: A bed filled with water.
examples: He has a waterbed.
The waterbed sloshes.
A waterbed is soft.

more.def: A bed with a mattress filled with water.
examples: He slept on a waterbed that sloshed when he moved.
The waterbed felt wavy.
A waterbed needs a strong frame.

easy.def: A paint mixed with water.
examples: I paint with watercolors.
The watercolor is wet.
She made a watercolor.

more.def: A paint mixed with water, or a picture painted with it.
examples: I painted a sunset with watercolors.
The watercolor picture hung in the hall.
She mixed blue watercolor on the paper.

easy.def: A small green plant that grows in water.
examples: Watercress is green.
We ate watercress.
Watercress grows in water.

more.def: A small plant with peppery leaves that grows in clear running water and is eaten in salads.
examples: Watercress grows along the bank of the stream.
She added watercress to the sandwich.
The soup was made with watercress.

easy.def: Water that falls over a high place.
examples: We saw a waterfall.
The waterfall is tall.
We swam by the waterfall.

more.def: A place where a river or stream drops from a high place, such as a cliff, to a lower one.
examples: We hiked to a tall waterfall deep in the forest.
The waterfall roared as it crashed onto the rocks below.
A rainbow shimmered in the mist of the waterfall.

easy.def: Birds that swim, like ducks.
examples: Ducks are waterfowl.
Waterfowl swim.
Geese are waterfowl.

more.def: Birds that live on or near water, such as ducks and geese.
examples: Ducks and geese are waterfowl.
The marsh was full of waterfowl.
Waterfowl have webbed feet for swimming.

easy.def: The part of a town beside the water.
examples: We walked on the waterfront.
The waterfront has boats.
The waterfront is busy.

more.def: The land beside a river, lake or sea, especially in a town.
examples: We walked along the waterfront and watched the boats.
The town built a park on the waterfront.
The restaurant on the waterfront has a view of the bay.

easy.def: A pool where animals drink.
examples: Zebras came to the waterhole.
The waterhole is small.
Animals drink at the waterhole.

more.def: A small pool of water where wild animals go to drink.
examples: Zebras and elephants gather at the waterhole.
The lions rested near the waterhole.
The waterhole dried up in summer.

easy.def: The line where the water meets the side of a boat.
examples: The waterline is low.
The boat sat low at the waterline.
Paint stops at the waterline.

more.def: The line along a boat's side up to which the water reaches.
examples: The ship sat low at the waterline.
Barnacles grew along the waterline.
The painter marked the waterline on the hull.

easy.def: Full of water.
examples: The ground was waterlogged.
A waterlogged boat.
The waterlogged shoes.

more.def: So full of water that it is heavy or soft.
examples: The ground was waterlogged after the storm.
Our shoes were waterlogged after the walk in the rain.
The waterlogged log sank.

easy.def: A faint mark in paper that shows when held to light.
examples: The paper has a watermark.
A watermark is a faint picture.
I saw a watermark.

more.def: A faint picture in paper.
examples: Hold the paper to the light to see the watermark.
Money paper has a watermark.
The watermark showed a tiny crown.

easy.def: A big, juicy fruit that is green outside and red inside.
examples: I ate watermelon.
The watermelon is sweet.
We cut the watermelon.

more.def: A large, round, juicy fruit with a hard green skin, sweet red flesh and many black seeds.
examples: We ate cold watermelon at the picnic on the hot summer day.
The watermelon was so big that I could not lift it.
He had a contest to see who could spit a watermelon seed the farthest.

easy.def: Not letting water in.
examples: My coat is waterproof.
The boots are waterproof.
I saw a waterproof bag.

more.def: Made so that water cannot get through.
examples: My waterproof coat kept me dry in the rain.
The boots are waterproof, so my feet stayed dry.
We put the map in a waterproof bag.

easy.def: An area where all the water flows to the same river or lake.
examples: A watershed drains water.
Rain in the watershed flows to the river.
It is in the watershed.

more.def: An area of land where all the rain and streams flow to the same river or lake.
examples: The town sits in the river's watershed.
Rain in the watershed flows into the lake.
Protecting the watershed keeps the water clean.

easy.def: A spinning storm over water.
examples: A waterspout twisted.
The waterspout spun.
We saw a waterspout.

more.def: A spinning column of water and wind over a lake or sea, like a tornado.
examples: A waterspout twisted over the bay.
Sailors fear a waterspout.
A waterspout spun across the sea.

easy.def: Not letting water in.
examples: The boat is watertight.
A watertight lid.
The bag is watertight.

more.def: Built so tightly that no water can get in or out.
examples: The boat is watertight, so it does not leak.
Use a watertight container for the lunch.
The tent was watertight in the rain.

easy.def: A river or path of water for boats.
examples: Boats use the waterway.
The waterway is wide.
We sailed the waterway.

more.def: A river, canal or other stretch of water that boats can travel along.
examples: Barges travel along the waterway.
The city grew up beside a wide waterway.
A waterway connects the two lakes.

easy.def: A big wheel turned by water.
examples: The waterwheel turned.
A waterwheel is big.
The waterwheel is by the river.

more.def: A large wheel that is turned by flowing water to power a mill.
examples: The waterwheel turned in the stream.
A waterwheel powered the old mill.
Water poured over the waterwheel.

easy.def: A place or system that supplies water to a town.
examples: The town has waterworks.
The waterworks cleans water.
Pipes run from the waterworks.

more.def: A system of buildings and pipes that supplies water to a town.
examples: The town's waterworks cleans the river water.
Pipes run from the waterworks to every house.
We toured the waterworks on a school trip.

easy.def: Like water, or thin.
examples: The soup is watery.
My eyes are watery.
A watery paint.

more.def: Full of water, or thin and weak like water.
examples: The soup was watery and had little taste.
My eyes were watery from the cold wind.
The paint was watery and ran down the paper.

easy.def: A unit that measures electric power.
examples: The bulb is sixty watts.
A watt measures power.
The lamp is fifty watts.

more.def: A unit used to measure how much electric power something uses.
examples: The light bulb uses sixty watts.
A hundred-watt bulb is brighter than a fifty-watt one.
The toaster uses a thousand watts.

easy.def: How much power something uses.
examples: The bulb's wattage is low.
Check the wattage.
High wattage.

more.def: The amount of electric power, measured in watts, that something uses.
examples: The bulb has a low wattage.
Check the wattage before you buy.
A heater has a high wattage.

easy.def: The loose skin hanging under a bird's chin.
examples: The turkey has a wattle.
A wattle is red.
The rooster's wattle.

more.def: The fleshy red skin hanging from the throat of a turkey or rooster.
examples: The turkey's red wattle shook.
The rooster has a bright wattle.
A wattle hangs under the chin.

easy.def: A moving hill of water.
examples: The wave hit the shore.
Big waves splash.
We jumped over the waves.

more.def: A moving ridge of water on the sea or a lake.
examples: The wave crashed against the rocks.
We jumped over the small waves.
Big waves pull the surfers out to sea.

easy.def: To move your hand to say hello or goodbye.
examples: I wave to my friend.
She waved goodbye.
He waves at the bus.

more.def: To move your hand back and forth to greet someone or say goodbye.
examples: The children waved to the bus driver.
She waved goodbye from the window.
He waved a flag at the parade.

easy.def: The distance between waves.
examples: The wavelength is short.
Sound has a wavelength.
Light has wavelengths.

more.def: The distance from one wave to the next, as in sound, light or water.
examples: Red light has a longer wavelength than blue.
The wavelength of the ocean wave was long.
Radio waves have different wavelengths.

easy.def: To shake or move back and forth.
examples: The candle wavered.
His voice wavered.
I did not waver.

more.def: To shake or move back and forth, or to be unsure.
examples: The candle flame wavered in the wind.
His voice wavered as he spoke.
She did not waver in her choice.

easy.def: Curvy like waves.
examples: Her hair is wavy.
A wavy line.
The wavy water moved.

more.def: Having a curved, up-and-down shape like waves.
examples: She has long, wavy hair.
He drew a wavy line across the page.
The wavy flag moved in the breeze.

easy.def: A soft stuff that candles are made of.
examples: The candle is made of wax.
The wax melted.
I polished the floor with wax.

more.def: A soft, oily substance that melts easily and is used for candles and polish.
examples: The candle was made of wax.
The hot wax dripped onto the plate.
Dad rubbed wax on the car.

easy.def: Pale like wax.
examples: A waxen face.
The waxen candle.
The waxen skin.

more.def: Pale like wax.
examples: His face looked waxen and pale.
The waxen candle melted.
Her skin was waxen.

easy.def: A path or road to get somewhere.
examples: This is the way to school.
Which way did the cat go?
The way home is short.

more.def: A road or path that leads somewhere, or the direction you go to get there.
examples: Can you tell me the way to the library?
The sign pointed the other way, so we turned around.
It is a long way to the top of the mountain.

easy.def: How you do something.
examples: I like your way of drawing.
Mom showed me a new way to tie shoes.
There is a way to fix it.

more.def: The method or manner in which something is done.
examples: There is more than one way to solve this math problem.
My grandfather has a funny way of laughing.
Birds find their way home by using the sun and the stars.

easy.def: The edge of a road.
examples: Flowers grew at the wayside.
We rested at the wayside.
The wayside was green.

more.def: The edge or side of a road or path.
examples: Wild flowers grew along the wayside.
We rested at the wayside under a tree.
A stone stood at the wayside.

easy.def: Hard to control.
examples: A wayward puppy ran.
The wayward ball rolled.
A wayward sheep strayed.

more.def: Hard to control, or likely to go the wrong way.
examples: A wayward puppy ran after the squirrel.
The wayward ball rolled into the street.
The shepherd found the wayward sheep.
